body:
ADR 0004 GRAIN-VOCABULARY REVIEW — recommendation: OPEN BUT PROTOCOL-SCOPED, not a closed narrative enum and not a generic declared integer. I inspected the draft and current source. BoundaryEvidence.level, BoundaryScore.level, and both BoundaryBeliefInput lookups use the integer as a key; story BoundaryBelief persists it; SegmentNode.level and NarrativeHierarchy.levelOf/descendantsAtLevel use a separate structural depth. The two-coordinate ruling is correct. The remaining choice needs a third refusal: situation/event/scene/episode is not a lawful perceptual vocabulary by itself because those names already denote resolved narrative ontology and would invite the exact B-to-A recycling this ADR forbids. A free integer plus prose is also insufficient because equality and map keying still assert comparability before the prose is consulted.

The perceptual identity should be the declared TASK-GRAIN pair, owned by a versioned protocol manifest. The protocol must carry the judgment axis and eligible anchor family, exact instruction/version/checksum, and the grain declaration. The grain may have a named open label and may expose an ordinal only when that one protocol explicitly declares a within-protocol order. No global ordering, equality, or weight lookup follows from equal labels or equal ordinals across protocols. BoundaryBeliefInput must therefore key by the full task-grain identity, never by grain alone.

SOURCE versus RECALL should share the abstract contract but not a comparison domain. Source-gap judgments and recall-turn/detail judgments have different anchor types and epistemic questions. The same word fine, event, or scene on both sides does not make the observations comparable. A domain discriminator in the protocol identity, preserved in codecs and receipts, is enough; duplicating two closed enums would only create parallel vocabularies that can drift. Any source-recall correspondence requires an explicit mapping artifact or alignment receipt.

StoryAtlas acceptance consequences make this judgeable before names/wire shape: (1) same exact gap under two instruction checksums remains two selectable tracks even if both say event; (2) equal ordinals under different protocols never merge or share weights; (3) track stacking uses only an explicit within-protocol order; (4) co-location with a resolved hierarchy bracket creates no cross-highlight without a FeatureUseLedger/resolver receipt; (5) source and recall tracks may synchronize spatially through declared mappings but never share identity. I recommend amending Sequencing step 2 to resolve the open question as protocol-scoped open identity with optional local order, and to reject both a global closed ontology and a globally comparable integer.
